classification.difficultyReason: Recognise how the complementary angle expressions combine into a constant quotient and connect that constant to the half-angle tangent value; the transformations are not specified.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{1}{1+\sqrt2}=\tan 22.5^\circ$.

Expand the differences and factor the numerator; use the double-angle formulas to identify the constant.
answer.worked:
Using $\sin45^\circ=\cos45^\circ=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}$,

$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\alpha+\sin(45^\circ-\alpha)}{\cos\alpha+\cos(45^\circ-\alpha)}&=\frac{\sin\alpha+\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(\cos\alpha-\sin\alpha)}{\cos\alpha+\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(\cos\alpha+\sin\alpha)}\\\frac{\sin\alpha+\sin(45^\circ-\alpha)}{\cos\alpha+\cos(45^\circ-\alpha)}&=\frac{(\sqrt2-1)\sin\alpha+\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha+(\sqrt2+1)\cos\alpha}\\\frac{\sin\alpha+\sin(45^\circ-\alpha)}{\cos\alpha+\cos(45^\circ-\alpha)}&=\frac{(\sqrt2-1)[\sin\alpha+(\sqrt2+1)\cos\alpha]}{\sin\alpha+(\sqrt2+1)\cos\alpha}\\\frac{\sin\alpha+\sin(45^\circ-\alpha)}{\cos\alpha+\cos(45^\circ-\alpha)}&=\sqrt2-1.\end{align*}$$

Set $\theta=22.5^\circ$, so $2\theta=45^\circ$. The double-angle formulas give

$$\begin{align*}\tan22.5^\circ&=\frac{2\sin22.5^\circ\cos22.5^\circ}{2\cos^2 22.5^\circ}\\\tan22.5^\circ&=\frac{\sin45^\circ}{1+\cos45^\circ}\\\tan22.5^\circ&=\frac{\sqrt2/2}{1+\sqrt2/2}\\\tan22.5^\circ&=\frac1{1+\sqrt2}=\sqrt2-1.\end{align*}$$

Hence the identity holds wherever the original quotient is defined.
